tender.title: Provision of Link 16 Network Management System (L16 NMS)
tender.description: The Situational Awareness Command and Control (SACC) Team, part of the UK Ministry of Defence intends to award a contract for the In-Service Support of a Link 16 Network Management System (NMS), with Thales UK Limited for a period of 2 years with options.

lots.description:
The United Kingdom (UK) Defence has an enduring requirement to manage and monitor all Link 16 activity within the UK and support up to 2 deployed operations. The NMS allows the Network Management operators to monitor network activity and modify the network architecture to provide optimal Link 16 network operating conditions. NMS also monitors all Link 16 activity to ensure compliance with the MOD/Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) UK Frequency Clearance Agreement (FCA).
The current equipment set up is unique and the software installed on the equipment is owned and supported by the Contractor. As the OEM with proprietary rights for the software that is installed on the equipment, support can only be provided by Thales UK Limited, as only they hold the technical information, tools and expertise required. In the immediate term changing the system would have a potentially detrimental impact and could result in an inability to utilise the Link 16 network across all platforms in the UK Flight Information Region (FIR). This would significantly curtail pan domain platform’s ability to train for operations.

options.description:

The contract contains options for out of hours support during crisis operations

tender.title: North Fawdon Primary School SuDS in Schools Scheme
tender.description:
Flooding on Dykefield in Fawdon was first brought to the attention of the LLFA in 2024. The land is owned by the Council but is managed by the Freemen of the City of Newcastle in the same way as the Town Moors. 
Following initial investigations and discussions with the school adjacent to Dykefield, North Fawdon Primary, it was established that previous flood events at the school had been caused by surface water run-off from Dykefield. Flooding to rear gardens of properties on Creswell Drive was also reported.
SuDS in Schools is a fund established by the Department for Education (DfE) to improve the resilience of schools to flooding issues by implementing Sustainable Drainage Systems (SuDS). The LLFA applied for funding and was informed it had been successful in 2025. DfE funding is for a maximum of 50% of any project. The Northumbria Regional Flood & Coast Committee has subsequently agreed to match fund the other 50% of successful DfE bids.
It is only practicable to undertake SuDS in Schools projects during the summer holidays, given the timescales involved in the construction of these projects and the need to minimize disruption to the school and safety issues for staff and pupils.
SuDS projects aim to manage storm water when conventional drainage systems are overwhelmed. Surface water is stored or "attenuated" in features like basins, swales or raingardens, which then slowly release water back into the environment once the peak of a storm has passed. As well reducing flood risk, features should be designed to deliver environmental, health and wellbeing and amenity benefits.

tender.description:
Street Lighting Maintenance Specification
Ellesmere Town Council are currently in the process of tendering the contract for the maintenance of the streetlights within the town for the next 3 years.
The Town Council has a lighting stock of 85 streetlights. Those that it was possible to convert (99%) were converted in 2020 to Holophane S-Line LED lights (dimmable and non-dimmable), Holophane Wall Packs, a Retrofit Lamp, Amenity Lantern, and a Philips Lumia Light.
The Council is inviting quotes for the following -
1)	A 'report only' contract for repairs. Faults will be reported to the contractor by Ellesmere Town Council and repaired within five working days. If repairs cannot be completed within this period, the Clerk is to be informed of the reasons and estimated repair timescales so that residents can be kept informed. 3)	An electrical inspection of all the Town Council's Street lighting (to comply with the current I.E.E.
Regulations). To be split over the 3 years of the contract.
Following the structural inspections, a comprehensive report must be provided to the Town Council together with the electrical test certificates and a list of suggested refurbishment works (and costs).
It is anticipated that the contractor who is awarded this contract will be the Town Council's preferred contractor for any maintenance work identified as a result of these inspections, however this is not guaranteed.
The contract will run for 3 years from 1st October 2026 and attached is the full contract specification and a list of the streetlights owned by the Town Council. The contract will be reviewed after the first year. All returned quotes must provide individual prices for repairs during the period of the contract. All invoices for payment must include a detailed breakdown of repairs and maintenance carried out in the period.

tender.title: Professional and Generic Skills Programme
tender.description:
NHS England intends to undertake a procurement for the design, delivery, administration and continuous improvement of a Professional and Generic Skills Programme for postgraduate medical and dental learners across the South West of England. The programme supports the development of leadership, management, communication, patient safety, ethics and quality improvement skills, aligned to the General Medical Council (GMC) Generic Professional Capabilities Framework and wider NHS workforce priorities. Approximately 225 learners are expected to participate each year. 
The future contract is expected to cover curriculum development, learner recruitment and administration, programme delivery, quality assurance, reporting and ongoing programme improvement. Delivery will be primarily virtual, with flexibility for blended delivery where appropriate. The proposed contract term is an initial three years with the option to extend for up to two further years. 
This preliminary market engagement exercise seeks feedback from potential providers, particularly higher education institutions and organisations experienced in postgraduate healthcare education. NHS England wishes to gather market intelligence to help refine the specification, understand market capability and capacity, identify potential delivery models, assess risks, and inform the forthcoming procurement strategy. Participation in this engagement exercise will not influence any future procurement process. 
NHS England has identified that learner demand may change during the life of the contract. Whilst the current requirement is based on approximately 225 learner places per year, the actual number of trainees participating in the programme may increase or decrease in response to workforce needs, funding availability and regional demand. Should a material change in learner numbers be required, any associated increase or decrease in contract value would be subject to budget availability, agreement between the parties, approval through NHS England governance processes, and any necessary business case approvals. 
NHS England has also identified that the curriculum may need to evolve during the contract term to reflect changes in regulatory requirements, national policy, professional standards, workforce priorities or updates to the General Medical Council's Generic Professional Capabilities Framework. The successful provider will be expected to work collaboratively with NHS England to review and update programme content where required, ensuring the curriculum remains current, compliant and aligned to emerging best practice. Any significant curriculum changes will be subject to appropriate governance and approval processes.
Suppliers are invited for market awareness and to provide feedback on draft documents. 
Further details and the supplier documents can be obtained from the following hyperlink.
https://health-family.force.com/s/Welcome

tender.title: The Provision of a Mental Health Crisis Text Support Service on behalf of NHS Cheshire and Merseyside Integrated Care Board
tender.description:
NHS Cheshire and Merseyside is seeking to engage with the market regarding the provision of an all-age, 24-hour, 7 days a week/ 365 days a year Mental Health Crisis Text Service across Cheshire and Merseyside.
The service will provide immediate, accessible and inclusive text-based support for individuals experiencing a mental health crisis and will operate 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. The service is intended to be fully integrated with NHS 111 (Mental Health Option) and local crisis response pathways, ensuring seamless access to urgent mental health support and onward referral where required.
The service has been developed in line with NHS England guidance on urgent and emergency mental health care and supports the objectives of the NHS Long Term Plan, the Urgent and Emergency Care Recovery Plan, and national suicide prevention priorities. It aims to improve access to crisis support for people who may experience barriers to traditional services, including those affected by stigma, communication difficulties, disability, sensory needs, or geographical isolation across the region's diverse urban and rural communities.
This notice is intended to inform the market of the Authority's future procurement intentions and support engagement with potential providers. 
The term of the contract is 2 years plus a potential 1 year extension. The total contract value over the 2 years plus the potential 1 year extension will be a maximum total contract value calculated as £900,000

lots.description:
The Authority is seeking to engage with the market in advance of a potential procurement for the provision of an all-age Mental Health Crisis Text Service across Cheshire and Merseyside, operating 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year.
The service will provide immediate text-based support for individuals experiencing mental health distress or crisis, including assessment, de-escalation, safety planning, signposting and referral into appropriate local crisis and urgent mental health services. The service must be accessible, inclusive and responsive to the needs of diverse populations, including individuals who may face barriers to accessing traditional telephone or face-to-face support.
The service will be required to integrate effectively with NHS 111 (Mental Health Option), local crisis pathways and other relevant health and care services across Cheshire and Merseyside, supporting timely access to urgent mental health care and helping to reduce avoidable presentations to emergency and acute services.
Through this market engagement exercise, the Authority is seeking feedback from potential providers on service delivery models, operational requirements, integration considerations, affordability, capacity and capability, and any opportunities for innovation. Information gathered will help inform the development of the service specification and procurement strategy.
All market engagement documentation and supporting materials will be made available via SAP Ariba. Interested organisations wishing to participate in this market engagement exercise should register their interest through SAP Ariba (link provided below), where they will be able to access the relevant documentation, submit responses and receive any updates or clarifications issued by the Authority.
https://portal.us.bn.cloud.ariba.com/dashboard/public/appext/comsapsbncdiscoveryui#/RfxEvent/preview/1110021195?anId=ANONYMOUS 
Please use the "Respond" button and follow the instructions provided to either log in or create an account.
Once this has been completed, you will be able to access and download the MEQ documents.
This procurement requirement falls within the scope of the Provider Selection Regime (PSR), as introduced under the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023. Accordingly, any subsequent procurement process will be conducted in accordance with the applicable PSR regulations and guidance. This market engagement exercise is being undertaken to inform the commissioning approach, understand market capability and capacity, and gather information from potential providers prior to making any procurement decision.

tender.title: Supported Housing - Resettlement and Community Support Service (RACSS)
tender.description:
Supported housing can be a powerful intervention in supporting people to remain independent in their own homes. The Authority is committed to and aims to build on its successful Supported Housing Programme through its service offer of short-term accommodation and support of up to 2 years, helping individuals maintain their independence, develop resilience, wellbeing and practical skills to sustain tenancies thus preventing homelessness, and offering resettlement enabling progression towards independent living. The specification builds on the long-standing services which were first delivered under the banner of Supporting People (SP). It retains the principles of supported housing established under SP and through subsequent commissioned services but takes advantage of the broader remit of the Authority as a housing authority. The contract will be delivered as one Lot covering the whole of North Yorkshire. The service aims to provide housing related support to enable high and medium level risk offenders supervised by the National Probation Service (NPS) to maximise their potential for independence, through sustaining accommodation, accessing, employment, preventing homelessness and significantly reducing the risks of harm and reoffending, whilst easing pressure on other statutory services, through collaboration at strategic, delivery, and case levels. 
The National Probation Service (NPS) will be involved in the Procurement and the ongoing Contract Management of this contract. 
***Please note that the published Contract Value is based on Year 1 tendered costs and tendered unit cost and a potential inflationary uplift at the Authority's discretion.***

tender.title: Supported Housing - Living Independently For Everyone (LIFE)
tender.description:
Supported housing can be a powerful intervention in enabling individuals to remain independent in their own homes. The Authority aims to build on its successful Supported Housing programme by enhancing and expanding its current service offer of short-term accommodation and support (1-2 years) helping individuals maintain independence, develop resilience, wellbeing and practical skills to sustain tenancies, prevent homelessness and hospital admissions, enabling them to progress towards recovery and independent living - whilst reducing pressures on statutory services. The specification builds on long-standing services from the Supporting People Programme and subsequent commissioned services, retaining core principles while taking advantage of the Authority's broader remit as a housing authority. It is ambitious in the vision to deliver a comprehensive supported housing offer for individuals with diverse physical and mental health needs linked to housing and homelessness, providing consistent, high quality, holistic, recovery focused accommodation and floating support across the Authority area. The expansion reflects changes in social care, broadening the focus beyond mental health to include individuals facing multiple disadvantage such as substance use, homelessness, autism, mild learning disabilities and other complex needs where short-term targeted housing support can enable independent living.
Preliminary market engagement has been carried out. Information is available at https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/043507-2025 Notice identifier: 2025/S 000-043507 The notice was unable to be linked due to the inclusion of Lots at tender stage following market engagement.

tender.title: Professional and Generic Skills Programme
tender.description:
NHS England intends to undertake a procurement for the design, delivery, administration and continuous improvement of a Professional and Generic Skills Programme for postgraduate medical and dental learners across the South West of England. The programme supports the development of leadership, management, communication, patient safety, ethics and quality improvement skills, aligned to the General Medical Council (GMC) Generic Professional Capabilities Framework and wider NHS workforce priorities. Approximately 225 learners are expected to participate each year. 
The future contract is expected to cover curriculum development, learner recruitment and administration, programme delivery, quality assurance, reporting and ongoing programme improvement. Delivery will be primarily virtual, with flexibility for blended delivery where appropriate. The proposed contract term is an initial three years with the option to extend for up to two further years. 
This preliminary market engagement exercise seeks feedback from potential providers, particularly higher education institutions and organisations experienced in postgraduate healthcare education. NHS England wishes to gather market intelligence to help refine the specification, understand market capability and capacity, identify potential delivery models, assess risks, and inform the forthcoming procurement strategy. Participation in this engagement exercise will not influence any future procurement process. 
NHS England has identified that learner demand may change during the life of the contract. Whilst the current requirement is based on approximately 225 learner places per year, the actual number of trainees participating in the programme may increase or decrease in response to workforce needs, funding availability and regional demand. Should a material change in learner numbers be required, any associated increase or decrease in contract value would be subject to budget availability, agreement between the parties, approval through NHS England governance processes, and any necessary business case approvals. 
NHS England has also identified that the curriculum may need to evolve during the contract term to reflect changes in regulatory requirements, national policy, professional standards, workforce priorities or updates to the General Medical Council's Generic Professional Capabilities Framework. The successful provider will be expected to work collaboratively with NHS England to review and update programme content where required, ensuring the curriculum remains current, compliant and aligned to emerging best practice. Any significant curriculum changes will be subject to appropriate governance and approval processes.
Suppliers are invited for market awareness and to provide feedback on draft documents. 
Further details and the supplier documents can be obtained from the following hyperlink.
https://health-family.force.com/s/Welcome

procedure.features:
1.1	STAGE 1 – Completeness Check & CoP & Tender Assessment
1.1.1	Participants must submit a completed Procurement Specific Question (PSQ) with their initial Tender submission.
1.1.2	Where a Participant is a consortium, all members of the consortium must complete a PSQ. The part of the PSQ concerning conditions of participation only requires to be completed by the lead member of the consortium.
1.2	Phase 1 – Completeness Check
1.2.1	The British Council will complete a check of all tender responses to ensure that they have been completed correctly and all necessary information has been provided. 
1.2.2	Tender responses correctly completed with all relevant information being provided, and all mandatory requirements, as set out in this ITT and associated documents, met; will proceed to Phase 2.  
1.2.3	Any tender responses not correctly completed in accordance with the requirements of this ITT and associated documents, and/or containing omissions may be rejected at this point.  Where a tender response is rejected at this point it will be rejected in full and not evaluated further and the supplier will automatically be disqualified from this Procurement Process.
1.3	Phase 2 – Excluded and Excludable
1.3.1	As detailed in Section 15 of the ITT document, British Council are required to exclude any Excluded suppliers from further participation in the event. Therefore, at this phase of the procurement, British Council will assess all Potential Suppliers for Mandatory Exclusion Grounds, and exclude any affected suppliers from further participation. Where a potential supplier is excluded at this point, its tender response will be rejected in full and not evaluated further and the supplier will automatically be disqualified from this Procurement Process.
1.3.2	As detailed in Section 15 of the ITT document, British Council may consider to exclude any Excludable suppliers from further participation in the event. Therefore, at this phase of the procurement, British Council will assess all Potential Suppliers for Discretionary Exclusion Grounds, and consider excluding any potential affected suppliers from further participation. Where a potential supplier is excluded at this point, its tender response will be rejected in full and not evaluated further and the supplier will automatically be disqualified from this Procurement Process.
1.4	Phase 3 – Conditions of Participation
1.4.1	British Council will check each potential supplier has completed the Procurement Specific Questionnaire correctly and in full.
1.4.2	Participants must also upload core supplier information to the Central Digital Platform and confirm to the Authority that they have done so.
1.4.3	British Council may request clarification and/or further information from Participants to gain a full and complete understanding of the submission.
1.4.4	British Council will assess each submission to confirm that the potential supplier meets all of the qualification criteria set out in the questionnaire, including the conditions of participation, as detailed in Section 16 of this ITT 
1.4.5	Potential suppliers that meet the qualification criteria will proceed to the next phase. 
1.4.6	Potential suppliers that do not meet the qualification criteria may be excluded from the Procurement Process at this point. Where a potential supplier is excluded at this point, its tender response will be rejected in full and not evaluated further and the supplier will automatically be disqualified from this Procurement Process.
1.5	Phase 4 – Assessment of Tenders
1.5.1	British Council will assess Responses from all potential suppliers who have passed Phase 1-3 of this process, to determine the most advantageous tender using the following criteria and weightings and will be assessed entirely on the response submitted:
1.5.2	Responses will be assessed using the Scoring Model outlined in paragraph 19.7 of this ITT.
Criteria	Weighting 
Social Value 	10%
Quality	[20]%
Methodology and Approach	[30]%
Commercial	[40]%
1.5.3	Moderation and application of weightings – The evaluation panel appointed for this procurement will meet to agree and moderate scores for each award criteria. Final scores in terms of a percentage of the overall tender score will be obtained by applying the relevant weighting factors set out as part of the award criteria table above. The percentage scores for each award criteria will be amalgamated to give a percentage score out of 100.

tender.title: Outsourcing services of Recruitment, Verification and Payroll Management of Workers (NPW) including examination venue staffs and Hourly paid teachers in Sri Lanka.
tender.description:
The British Council in Sri Lanka is inviting reputable and experienced outsourcing services providing vendors to submit tenders for providing  verification and payroll management of various categories of Non-Permanent Workers (NPW) through an employee placement agency who has experience in providing end to end staffing solutions and  management of  payroll for Exam venue staffs and Teachers for the British Council Sri Lanka.
The British Council Sri Lanka facilitates a comprehensive array of UK qualifications throughout Sri Lanka via our offices in Colombo, Kandy, and Jaffna, as well as in the Maldives. We administer exams in several cities across Sri Lanka and in Malé, Maldives, totalling approximately 100,000 exams annually. Also, we have Teaching Centres in all Colombo, Kandy, Jaffna & Matara Branch offices with a total number of teachers counting to over 75. 
To deliver these exams, we require about 500 exams venue staffs and examiners in Sri Lanka, including Chief Supervisors, Assistant Supervisors, Invigilators, Marshals, Temporary Back-office Staff, and Examiners. Given the scale of these contractual relationships and payroll activities, which extend beyond the core responsibilities of our specialized exams delivery team, we have outsourced the management and payment of venue staff and hourly paid teachers’ contracts, verification and Payroll management of Exams venue staffs and Teachers. We can handover the existing pool of venue staffs and teachers so that the vendor needs to manage the payroll only on monthly basis and in such scenario, there will be no payment for recruitment and verification.

tender.title: the Development and Delivery of Armagh City, Banbridge and Craigavon Borough Council Local Economic Partnership  Productivity Growth Programme 2026-28
tender.description:
Armagh City, Banbridge and Craigavon Borough Council invites tenders from experienced providers to deliver the Productivity Growth Programme, to micro, small, and social enterprises (up to 50 employees). This programme forms an important part of the work of the LEP under the priority theme Supporting Business Growth. 
The programme is designed to improve business productivity, resilience and long-term growth by identifying productivity challenges, providing tailored mentoring support, and creating clear progression pathways for continued business development. The appointed delivery agent will be responsible for recruiting eligible businesses, undertaking detailed productivity diagnostics, delivering targeted mentoring interventions, and supporting businesses to access wider growth, investment and scaling opportunities.
